blocks.text: CEBU CITY, Philippines — Despite falling short of their first-ever Professional Chess Association of the Philippines (PCAP) Wesley So Cup championship, the Toledo Xignex Trojans have plenty of reasons to celebrate after another impressive season. Team co-owner and lawyer Jeah Gacang expressed pride and gratitude over the Trojans’ performance, saying their consistency over the years speaks volumes about the team’s dedication, competitive spirit, and commitment. “Not the ending we prayed for, but still a journey worth celebrating,” Gacang said in a statement following Toledo’s narrow defeat to Manila AQ Prime Assets in the championship showdown on Wednesday night, November 25. “Of course, […]...
